body.text: No surgical procedure is risk-free, whether performed in London, New York, or Istanbul. The [UK FCDO Turkey travel advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health) and [GOV.UK Travel Aware surgery abroad guidance](https://travelaware.campaign.gov.uk/surgery-abroad-cut-out-the-risk/) emphasize planning for unexpected clinical events before you leave home rather than improvising during an emergency. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about), our two founders operate on a client-paid, flat-fee model—paid by our clients and independent of provider commissions—so our loyalty sits solely with you when plans change. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.
What should be in your written complication protocol before you ever board a flight?

A practical complication protocol fits on two printed pages carried in your cabin folder and shared with your travel companion or home emergency contact. It must list your operating hospital's 24/7 emergency desk, your surgeon's direct clinical escalation line, your complication insurer's emergency authorization number, your embassy helpline, and your home GP's contact details.

Both the [NHS cosmetic surgery abroad guide](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/advice/cosmetic-surgery-abroad/) and the [British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons (BAAPS)](https://baaps.org.uk/patients/safety_in_surgery/cosmetic_tourism.aspx) warn that home public health systems generally cover life-threatening emergencies only—not routine wound revisions or delayed follow-up care. Prepare these core items before departure:

items: Signed hospital complication policy: Written terms stating what revision surgery, imaging, antibiotics, or extra inpatient nights are covered—and what costs fall on the patient.
Full English clinical record plan: Confirmation that you will receive operative notes, implant serial numbers, pathology reports, and medication charts before discharge.
24/7 clinical escalation numbers: Direct hospital emergency department phone and Turkish emergency ambulance number (112), not just a sales coordinator's WhatsApp.
Financial & flight buffer: A flexible return ticket and accessible credit limit to cover unexpected hotel nights before insurance reimbursement clears.

body.text: How do accredited Turkish hospitals handle unplanned readmissions?

Full-service private hospitals accredited by [Joint Commission International (JCI)](https://www.jointcommissioninternational.org/about-jci/accredited-organizations/) and licensed on the [Turkish Ministry of Health authorized healthcare providers directory](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html) maintain 24/7 emergency departments, on-site imaging, blood banks, and intensive care units (ICUs). If bleeding, infection, or severe dehydration occurs after hotel discharge, an accredited hospital can admit you directly under your surgical team.

Problems most often arise when patients book low-cost outpatient clinics that lack overnight beds or ICU backup, forcing an ambulance transfer to a separate public or private hospital that has no access to your operative notes. Always confirm in writing that your procedure takes place inside a licensed multi-specialty hospital with on-site ICU capability.
Why is specialist complication insurance non-negotiable for surgery abroad?

Standard holiday travel insurance almost universally excludes medical emergencies resulting from planned elective surgery abroad. As the Australian [Smartraveller medical tourism guide](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/travel-essentials/travel-health/medical-tourism) advises, travelling without dedicated medical travel cover can expose you to tens of thousands of euros in inpatient care, revision procedures, extended accommodation, or medical repatriation.

body.text: Dedicated providers—such as [Medical Travel Shield](https://www.medicaltravelshield.com/) for international travellers or Turkish health-tourism complication policies issued through licensed insurers—must be purchased before your procedure date and verified for your exact surgery type.
What role does ITO's local team play if an unplanned stay extension happens?

When a surgeon advises staying an extra three to seven nights for IV antibiotics, drain removal, or wound monitoring, the stress of rebooking hotels, flights, and transport hits immediately. Through our [medical tourism coordination service](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism), our local team in Türkiye steps in to handle every non-clinical change: extending your current recovery hotel room (or relocating you closer to the hospital), coordinating pharmacy pickups, adjusting airport transfers, and rebooking flexible flights once your doctor signs new fit-to-fly paperwork.

If you want a realistic, safety-first itinerary with flexible accommodation and local Istanbul backup, reach out via our [medical tourism coordination page](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism) or learn how our two founders work on our [About page](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about). Please do not send passport or ID scans, medical records, or payment details in your first enquiry—just share your planned dates and logistical questions so we can explain how we support your stay.

faq.q: Will my home country's public health system fix a complication from surgery abroad?
faq.a: Public systems such as the NHS typically treat immediate life-threatening emergencies, but they generally do not cover non-urgent cosmetic revisions, routine wound checks, or elective corrective procedures.

faq.q: Does Turkish law require clinics to offer complication insurance?
faq.a: Turkish health tourism regulations require authorized providers to operate within strict licensing frameworks, and many surgical packages include a local complication policy. Always read the actual insurance certificate—coverage periods and exclusions vary widely.

faq.q: Should I fly home early if I feel unwell after discharge?
faq.a: No. Boarding a flight with fever, uncontrolled pain, calf swelling, or heavy wound drainage can turn a manageable issue into an in-flight medical emergency. Contact your surgical team in Istanbul immediately for an in-person review.

faq.q: What documents do I need if I have to visit a doctor after returning home?
faq.a: Carry your full English operative report, anesthesia record, lab results, implant or device cards, and discharge medication list so any clinician at home knows exactly what was performed.

faq.q: Can Itinerary of Türkiye negotiate medical refunds or give clinical second opinions?
faq.a: No. We are a non-clinical travel advisory, not a medical practice or law firm. We manage your accommodation extensions, transport, and local logistics while you and your licensed medical team handle clinical decisions.

faq.q: How much financial buffer should I keep available for an unexpected stay extension?
faq.a: Keeping an accessible emergency buffer of €1,500 to €3,000 (or equivalent credit) alongside specialist complication insurance helps cover immediate hotel extensions and flight-change differences without delay while claims are processed.
